name: Cerebrolysin

what.text: Cerebrolysin is a mixture of small peptides and amino acids taken from pig brain protein. It is not a single molecule.

what.text: It is made by EVER Neuro Pharma in Unterach, Austria. It is a solution given by injection into a muscle or a vein, or as an infusion into a vein. Each millilitre holds 215.2 mg of Cerebrolysin concentrate.

what.text: In Austria it is an approved medicine. Its leaflet says it is used in adults and older patients to support treatment of disorders of the brain's blood vessels, in particular Alzheimer-type and vascular dementia, deficits after stroke, and brain injury (concussion and contusion).

what.text: How it might act in people is not settled. Cochrane's review of stroke trials found it probably makes little or no difference to death.

research.text: Cerebrolysin has been tested in many randomized trials, mostly in stroke and dementia, and several were funded by its maker. Cochrane's 2023 stroke review found it probably makes little or no difference to death, with a possible rise in non-fatal serious adverse events. Cochrane's 2019 dementia review rated the evidence very low quality.

research.title: Acute ischaemic stroke, Cochrane 2023

facts.v: Ziganshina LE, et al. Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2023;10:CD007026
review of randomized controlled trials starting within 48 hours of stroke, against placebo or no treatment
7 trials, 1,773 participants; one of these tested Cortexin, a similar product from cattle brain
death from any cause, serious adverse events, all adverse events

research.found: Death: probably little or no difference (risk ratio 0.96; moderate certainty). Serious adverse events overall: probably little or no difference. Non-fatal serious adverse events: more common with Cerebrolysin (risk ratio 2.39; moderate certainty). No trial reported death or dependence at the end of follow-up, or quality of life. The maker supported three of the trials.

src.label: Ziganshina et al., Cochrane review: Cerebrolysin for acute ischaemic stroke, 2023

research.title: Vascular dementia, Cochrane 2019

facts.v: Cui S, et al. Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2019;(11):CD008900
review of randomized controlled trials
6 trials, 597 participants, mostly mild to moderate vascular dementia, in China, Russia and Romania
15 days to three years of follow-up
thinking scores (MMSE, ADAS-cog+), global function, deaths, adverse events

research.found: Small gains on thinking and global scores, rated very low-quality evidence. The reviewers wrote that the evidence base is weak and that any benefit may be too small to matter clinically. All trials with funding details were industry-supported.

research.title: CASTA: acute stroke in Asia

facts.v: Heiss WD, et al. Stroke 2012;43(3):630-6; NCT00868283
EVER Neuro Pharma
1,070 patients with acute ischaemic stroke, treated within 12 hours: 529 on Cerebrolysin, 541 on placebo
30 mL Cerebrolysin or saline by drip, once a day for 10 days, with aspirin
90 days of follow-up
a combined score of modified Rankin Scale, Barthel Index and NIH Stroke Scale

research.found: No difference on the main outcome. In a later look at patients with severe strokes, the authors saw a trend favouring Cerebrolysin and said it needed a new trial to confirm.

research.title: CARS: recovery after stroke

facts.v: Muresanu DF, et al. Stroke 2016;47(1):151-9; EudraCT 2007-000870-21
several authors worked for EVER Neuro Pharma
208 patients after stroke: 104 on Cerebrolysin, 104 on placebo
30 mL Cerebrolysin or saline once a day for 21 days, starting 24 to 72 hours after stroke, with a rehabilitation program
90 days
Action Research Arm Test (arm and hand function) at day 90

research.found: Arm function scores were higher with Cerebrolysin. The authors called the study exploratory and small, and said a large trial should confirm it.

side.text: From the Austrian leaflet: allergic reactions, seizures, agitation, and fast heartbeat or dizziness when given too fast. It must not be used during an epileptic seizure or with severe kidney failure. Cochrane found more non-fatal serious adverse events with Cerebrolysin in stroke trials.

items.text: allergy to Cerebrolysin; an epileptic seizure; severe kidney failure. Extra care is advised with allergies and with epilepsy, where seizures may become more frequent.

items.text: allergic reactions including tingling, skin and blood-vessel reactions, neck, head and limb pain, fever, back pain, shortness of breath, chills and a shock-like state. Single grand mal seizures and one convulsion have been linked to it. Fast injection can cause palpitations or heart-rhythm problems in single cases. Also indigestion, diarrhoea, constipation, vomiting and nausea.

UK (MHRA), Australia's TGA register and national agencies in EU countries other than Austria were not checked.
surprises: Cerebrolysin is widely used for stroke in several countries, yet Cochrane's 2023 review found it probably makes no difference to death and may increase non-fatal serious adverse events.
CARS, a small maker-linked trial, reported a large benefit on arm function, while CASTA, a trial of 1,070 patients, found no difference on its main outcome.
